free_tier.stated: 'Please, fill in this form to get your FREE IPv6 tunnel.' The form asks for an email and 'IPv4 address of your side of the tunnel'.

egress.terms: 'We provide our service free of charge.' No traffic allowance, rate or fair-use clause is published.; ingress: udp

interface_detail: a web form for registration and an HTTP auto-update URL for a dynamic endpoint address
tooling: unknown until the protocol is known; iproute2 for a 6in4 tunnel, wg-quick if WireGuard exists
chaining: would compose with a free VM the same way Route64 does, if the protocol turns out to be routable
binding_note: No quota, rate or object cap is published, so nothing in the vocabulary fails at 1 TiB/month. What is unproven is whether the tunnel can carry the traffic at all, which is a protocol question rather than a limit.

identity_cost.detail: 'E-mail (will be your login)'. No card, phone or national identity is asked for. The vendor warns against hotmail and live.com addresses because mail to them is blocked.

reliability_note: mail to hotmail and live.com addresses is blocked by the mail provider, so a password may never arrive; support is one address and a phone number in Kyiv.
confidence_note: The free tunnel and the IPv4 endpoint shape are documented. The protocol, the prefix size and whether WireGuard is offered at all were not established: reading the FAQ and help paths returned 404, and the account pages need a login. One vendor sentence naming the tunnel type and prefix would raise this to documented.

evidence.proved: free registration, the auto-update endpoint for a dynamic IPv4, and 'We provide our service free of charge.'
'Please, fill in this form to get your FREE IPv6 tunnel.' and the two fields a new account supplies

notes: Recorded as unverified because W test cannot be answered from the vendor's pages. The site is a 2011-era broker with an email login, an IPv4 endpoint field and a dynamic-IP updater, which is the classic protocol-41 shape described in the Wikipedia tunnel broker article; that is inference, not evidence. The 1 TiB question is unanswerable until the protocol is known, because a proto-41 tunnel is capped by the endpoint's own uplink while a routed prefix is capped by the broker's policy.

extras.wg_detail: No page read names the tunnel protocol. WireGuard is not mentioned on the front page, the registration page, or either FAQ path tried (both returned 404). The endpoint field is an IPv4 address, which is the 6in4 or GRE shape.
extras.volume_stated: 'We provide our service free of charge.' No traffic allowance, rate or fair-use clause is published.
extras.transit_note: NetAssist carries the tunnel from its Ukrainian network
